candidats.titre: File:Close-up of a Regenerative Turbine Pump Impeller inside of a T51 Series pump from MTH Pumps.jpg
candidats.description: This is a close up of the inner workings of an MTH T51 Series Regenerative Turbine Pump. Fluid is introduced from the inlet side (Right) as the impeller rotates clockwise. The fluid is pushed in a helical pattern split between both sides of the impeller. As it spins through the fluid path (water channel) it increases pressure until it hits the water stop and exits out of the discharge side of the pump (Left) at a much higher pressure, but only moderate to low flows.

candidats.titre: File:Casing of a main circulation pump from the Greifswald Nuclear Power Plant.jpg
candidats.description: The massive austenitic steel casing of a main circulation pump (Hauptumwälzpumpe ), a component from a decommissioned VVER-440 reactor at the Greifswald Nuclear Power Plant in Lubmin. This pump was a vertical, single-stage centrifugal pump. A small information plate on the casing indicates its weight is approximately 11 tons and it was manufactured in 1989. These pumps were essential for circulating the primary coolant through the reactor core, with a flow rate of 7100 m³/h at a design pressure of 14 MPa and a temperature of 335°C
